message:
test: collect orphaned MessagePortMain with a precise GC in the close-event spec (#54191)

test: collect orphaned MessagePortMain and reply channels with a precise GC

v8Util.requestGarbageCollectionForTesting() runs the collection synchronously,
so the unified heap scans the native stack conservatively. When the request is
made from inside an IPC handler, the frames that just entangled an incoming
MessagePortMain (or created an invoke reply channel) can leave a stale pointer
on that stack, and cppgc then keeps the object alive. A heap snapshot taken at
that point shows the port retained only by "C++ native stack roots", and under
UBSan the "close event ... sent to nowhere" spec failed most runs because the
port was never reclaimed.

Add an { execution: 'async' } option that posts the collection as a
non-nestable task and runs it with StackState::kNoHeapPointers, mirroring
gc({ execution: 'async' }) from --expose-gc, and use it in the two specs that
assert a C++ object is reclaimed after a single collection.
